CHIEF COMPLAINT
Recurrent kidney stone with history of hypertension and diabetes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female presenting with recurrent kidney stones. She reports experiencing pain that has been intermittent and presented to the emergency room last week. She believes the stone has passed approximately three days ago. She denies current blood in urine and denies current pain. At the ER, she was given pain medication, which she recalls was Percocet. This represents approximately her seventh or eighth kidney stone episode. She has seen a urologist previously, approximately one year ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain. Patient denies abdominal pain. Patient reports history of insomnia with occasional difficulty sleeping due to worry. She has tried meditation apps which provide some benefit. She denies current use of television or phone during sleep. She has tried melatonin a couple of times without significant benefit.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Recurrent kidney stones (approximately 7-8 episodes)
2. Hypertension
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
4. Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (known, unchanged)
5. Insomnia

MEDICATIONS
1. Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
2. Metformin 500 mg daily
3. Percocet (recently given at ER)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports busy lifestyle on the go. She struggles with diet, particularly consuming fast food, cakes, and cookies. She acknowledges difficulty giving up fast food due to time constraints and limited time for meal preparation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur present, unchanged from previous exam
Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation
Costovertebral angle (CVA): No tenderness to palpation bilaterally

RESULTS
Blood pressure at visit: 150/90 mmHg
Home blood pressure readings: 130-140/60-70 mmHg
A1C from last visit: 6.7% (slightly elevated, improved from initial diagnosis)
Physical exam findings: Lungs clear, known systolic ejection murmur present without worsening, abdomen and CVA non-tender

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Recurrent kidney stones: Patient has passed current stone. Likely white coat hypertension contributing to elevated BP at visit. Recommend urinalysis and urine culture to rule out infection. Referral to urology (specifically requesting Dr. Harris) for evaluation of recurrent stone formation and underlying etiology.

2. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Home readings show improvement from initial 180 mmHg. Continue current medication without changes. No refills needed at this time. Refer to nutrition for dietary counseling to reduce sodium intake to less than 2300 mg daily.

3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Patient encouraged to check blood glucose before meals to assess dietary intake appropriately. A1C trending in right direction; continue monitoring.

4. Insomnia: Patient prefers non-pharmacological approaches but willing to try medication. Start Melatonin 10 mg as needed. Reinforce sleep hygiene recommendations including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and using iPhone sleep mode if available to minimize disruptions.

5. Nutrition consultation arranged to address dietary modifications and support weight management goals.

Follow-up appointment in 3 months.
